title: Differential Equations
description: Differential Equations develops the language of change over time and space. The unified course serves various degree pathways through a common mathematical spine: formulation, analytical solution, qualitative reasoning, numerical approximation, validation, and interpretation. Discipline-specific examples change, but expectations for reasoning and communication remain consistent.

resources.title: Elementary Differential Equations and Boundary Value Problems
resources.description: Boyce, DiPrima, and Meade. Balanced core text for analytical methods, modeling, systems, series, numerical methods, and boundary-value problems.

resources.title: Differential Equations and Boundary Value Problems
resources.description: Edwards, Penney, and Calvis. Accessible engineering-oriented development with broad application coverage.

resources.title: Differential Equations
resources.description: Blanchard, Devaney, and Hall. Strong qualitative, numerical, and dynamical-systems viewpoint.

resources.title: Ordinary Differential Equations
resources.description: Tenenbaum and Pollard. Deep problem-solving reference and historical Dover resource.

resources.title: Nonlinear Dynamics and Chaos
resources.description: Strogatz. Excellent enrichment for phase lines, nonlinear systems, bifurcations, oscillations, and chaos.

resources.title: Mathematical Physiology
resources.description: Keener and Sneyd. Biomedical enrichment for compartment, transport, feedback, and physiological models.

resources.title: MIT OpenCourseWare 18.03SC Differential Equations
resources.description: Complete independent-study course with notes, videos, problems, solutions, and exams.

resources.title: MIT OpenCourseWare ES.1803 Differential Equations (Spring 2024)
resources.description: Recent topic notes and syllabus extending through Fourier series, PDE separation, and qualitative systems.

resources.title: Paul's Online Math Notes - Differential Equations
resources.description: Concise explanations and worked practice for standard ODE methods.

resources.title: LibreTexts Differential Equations
resources.description: Open textbooks covering analytical, numerical, systems, and modeling topics.

resources.title: Khan Academy Differential Equations
resources.description: Guided review and practice for foundational solution techniques and transforms.

resources.title: UC Berkeley Math 54
resources.description: Useful benchmark for the linear-algebra, systems, eigenvalue, and Fourier connections.

resources.title: Python: SciPy solve_ivp and solve_bvp
resources.description: Open numerical IVP/BVP solvers. Pair with NumPy, Matplotlib, and SymPy for verification. Also https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.integrate.solve_bvp.html.

resources.title: MATLAB ODE solvers
resources.description: Widely used engineering solver family with event handling and stiff-system options.

resources.title: Julia DifferentialEquations.jl
resources.description: High-performance ecosystem for ODE, SDE, DAE, and PDE-related scientific computing.

resources.title: GeoGebra or Desmos
resources.description: Quick direction-field, slope, and solution-curve explorations for conceptual checks. Also https://www.desmos.com/.

resources.title: Professor Leonard - Differential Equations
resources.description: Long-form classroom lectures and worked examples.

resources.title: 3Blue1Brown - Differential Equations
resources.description: Visual intuition for differential equations, exponentials, systems, and physical models.

resources.title: MIT OpenCourseWare YouTube
resources.description: Lecture and problem-solving videos aligned with MIT differential equations materials.

resources.title: Steve Brunton
resources.description: Applied dynamical systems, state-space modeling, control, and data-driven computation.

resources.title: Dr. Trefor Bazett
resources.description: Clear short-form explanations of ODE methods and phase-plane ideas.

topics.title: Differential-Equation Models, Direction Fields, and Well-Posed Problems
topics.description: Differential equations turn local laws of change into predictions about an evolving system. This opening unit teaches students to formulate models, read solution geometry, and ask whether an initial-value problem has a meaningful and unique solution before calculating.

children.title: Modeling and classification
children.description: Classification reveals what kind of mathematical object is being studied and which tools might apply.

children.title: Dependent and independent variables, parameters, state variables, and units
Ordinary versus partial differential equations, order, linearity, autonomy
Initial-value and boundary-value problems
Translating conservation, balance, force, circuit, kinetic, and population laws into equations
Direction fields and solution curves
children.description: A direction field displays the slopes prescribed by a first-order equation and reveals behavior even when no closed form exists.

children.title: Isoclines, nullclines, integral curves, and families of solutions
Reading monotonicity, equilibria, and long-run trends from a field
Matching equations, direction fields, and candidate solution graphs
Technology-assisted plots with interpretation rather than visual guesswork
Existence, uniqueness, and validation
children.description: A solution method matters only when the mathematical problem is well posed and the result survives basic reality checks.

children.title: Local existence and uniqueness for y'=f(t,y) under standard continuity conditions
Intervals of existence, singularities, and nonunique behavior
Verification by substitution and initial or boundary data
Dimensional consistency, limiting cases, signs, magnitudes, and model assumptions

topics.title: First-Order Differential Equations and Analytical Methods
topics.description: First-order equations describe one state variable whose rate depends on time, the state, or both. Students learn a decision process for recognizing structure and selecting a method instead of treating formulas as an unconnected catalog.

children.title: Separable equations
children.description: Separation isolates the variables so that antidifferentiation converts a rate law into an implicit or explicit solution.

children.title: Separating variables and integrating both sides
Applying initial conditions and determining solution intervals
Implicit solutions, equilibrium solutions, and lost solutions
Growth, decay, cooling, reaction-rate, and drag models
Linear equations and integrating factors
children.description: The integrating factor turns a first-order linear equation into a product derivative and exposes the roles of forcing and initial data.

children.title: Standard form y'+p(t)y=g(t)
Deriving and applying the integrating factor
Homogeneous response, particular response, and superposition
Mixing, circuits, pharmacokinetics, and input-output models
Exact equations and useful substitutions
children.description: Exactness recognizes a hidden potential function, while substitutions convert certain nonlinear equations into familiar types.

children.title: Differential forms M dx + N dy = 0 and the exactness test
Recovering a potential function and applying initial data
Bernoulli equations and homogeneous first-order substitutions
Choosing methods through structural cues and checking the result

topics.title: Autonomous Equations, Qualitative Analysis, and Nonlinear Models
topics.description: Autonomous equations show how a system changes as a function of its current state. Their phase-line geometry often tells more about equilibria, stability, thresholds, and long-run behavior than an explicit formula does.

children.title: Phase lines and stability
children.description: A phase line compresses the dynamics of y'=f(y) into equilibria and arrows that describe how solutions move.

children.title: Equilibria and sign charts for f(y)
Stable, unstable, and semistable equilibria
Basins of attraction and dependence on initial conditions
Bifurcation awareness when a parameter changes the equilibrium pattern
Canonical nonlinear models
children.description: Simple nonlinear laws capture saturation, competition, thresholds, and feedback that pure exponential models miss.

children.title: Logistic growth and carrying capacity
Harvesting, ignition, threshold, and limited-resource models
Compartment, mixing, reaction, and elimination models
Nondimensionalization and interpretation of parameter groups
Model calibration and critique
children.description: A model is an argument about mechanisms, not merely an equation, so students must connect parameters to data and limitations.

children.title: Estimating parameters from initial rates, equilibria, half-lives, or data
Comparing models using residuals and qualitative behavior
Sensitivity to parameters and initial conditions
Communicating assumptions, validity ranges, and uncertainty

topics.title: Numerical Solution of Initial-Value Problems
topics.description: Most realistic differential equations do not have elementary closed-form solutions. Numerical methods approximate trajectories while making step size, stability, error, and verification part of the mathematical reasoning.

children.title: Euler and improved Euler methods
children.description: Euler's method advances along local tangent lines and makes the logic of time stepping transparent.

children.title: Forward Euler update and geometric interpretation
Heun or midpoint methods as second-order improvements
Step-size studies and global versus local truncation error
Failure near steep gradients, singularities, or unstable dynamics
Runge-Kutta methods and solver practice
children.description: Runge-Kutta methods combine several slope estimates to achieve strong accuracy without higher derivatives.

children.title: Classical fourth-order Runge-Kutta structure
Adaptive step size, error tolerances, and event detection
Using Python, MATLAB, or Julia solvers responsibly
Reproducible plots, labeled axes, units, and solver settings
Error, stability, and verification
children.description: A computed curve is evidence only after its convergence and consistency have been checked.

children.title: Comparing against exact solutions or conserved quantities
Refinement studies and empirical convergence
Numerical stability versus stability of the continuous model
Stiffness awareness and when explicit methods struggle

topics.title: Higher-Order Linear Differential Equations
topics.description: Higher-order linear equations govern oscillations, beams, circuits, control elements, and many reduced physical models. Their solution structure separates the system's natural behavior from the effects of forcing.

children.title: Linear theory and solution spaces
children.description: The theory of linear equations explains why homogeneous solutions form a vector space and how initial data select one trajectory.

children.title: Linear differential operators and homogeneous versus nonhomogeneous equations
Existence and uniqueness for linear initial-value problems
Linear independence, the Wronskian, and fundamental solution sets
Superposition and the dimension of an nth-order solution space
Constant-coefficient homogeneous equations
children.description: Characteristic roots turn differentiation into algebra and connect root structure to growth, decay, and oscillation.

children.title: Distinct real roots, repeated roots, and complex conjugate roots
Euler's formula and real-valued oscillatory solutions
Initial-condition systems and interpretation of constants
Mechanical, electrical, and chemical examples
Reduction of order and variable coefficients
children.description: When one solution is known or coefficients vary, reduction techniques extend the core linear framework.

children.title: Reduction of order for a second independent solution
Cauchy-Euler equations and power-law trial forms
Abel's identity and qualitative information from the Wronskian
Recognizing when numerical or series methods are more appropriate

topics.title: Forced Systems, Oscillations, and Response Methods
topics.description: Forcing introduces energy or information into a linear system. This unit connects solution methods to transient and steady-state response, damping, resonance, frequency response, and physically meaningful design decisions.

children.title: Undetermined coefficients
children.description: For common forcing functions, a trial response can be selected from a family preserved by differentiation.

children.title: Polynomial, exponential, sinusoidal, and combined inputs
Trial-form selection and the modification rule for resonance
Complementary and particular solutions
Applicability limits when coefficients are not constant or forcing is irregular
Variation of parameters
children.description: Variation of parameters constructs a particular solution from a fundamental homogeneous basis and works for much broader forcing.

children.title: Deriving the parameter equations under a simplifying constraint
Wronskian formulas for second-order equations
Definite-integral forms that incorporate initial conditions
Comparison with Green-function and convolution ideas
Oscillation, damping, and resonance
children.description: Second-order response models show how system parameters control natural frequency, decay, amplitude, and phase.

children.title: Undamped, underdamped, critically damped, and overdamped motion
Driven oscillations, beats, pure resonance, and practical resonance
Amplitude gain, phase lag, and frequency-response curves
Mass-spring-damper, RLC circuit, structural, and physiological analogies

topics.title: Laplace Transforms, Impulses, and Transfer Functions
topics.description: The Laplace transform converts differential equations into algebraic equations while handling initial data and discontinuous inputs naturally. It also introduces the language of impulse response and transfer functions used across engineering and applied science.

children.title: Transform fundamentals
children.description: The transform records a time-domain function as a complex-frequency representation whose algebra can simplify initial-value problems.

children.title: Definition, convergence idea, linearity, and common transform pairs
First and second shifting theorems
Transforms of derivatives and incorporation of initial conditions
Partial fractions and inverse transforms
Steps, impulses, and convolution
children.description: Generalized and piecewise inputs model switches, shocks, injections, collisions, and short-duration forcing.

children.title: Heaviside step functions and piecewise input construction
Dirac delta as an idealized impulse and jump conditions
Convolution and the response to a general input
Impulse response as a system fingerprint
Transfer functions and system response
children.description: A transfer function links input to output and reveals stability and frequency behavior through its poles and zeros.

children.title: Zero-state and zero-input response
Poles, zeros, stability, and damping interpretation
Block-diagram and input-output viewpoints
Connections to circuits, control, signal processing, transport, and pharmacokinetics

topics.title: Linear Systems of Differential Equations
topics.description: Coupled systems describe interacting states and provide the natural language for multicomponent engineering, chemical, biological, and physical models. Eigenvalues and eigenvectors translate matrix structure into modes of motion.

children.title: System formulation and matrix methods
children.description: Writing x'=Ax+g(t) exposes coupling and permits a unified treatment of many higher-order and compartment models.

children.title: Converting higher-order equations to first-order systems
State vectors, system matrices, and equilibrium points
Fundamental matrices and the matrix exponential
Existence, uniqueness, and superposition for linear systems
Eigenvalue solution methods
children.description: Eigenpairs identify invariant modes whose growth, decay, and rotation build the general solution.

children.title: Distinct real eigenvalues and modal decomposition
Complex eigenvalues and spiral or center behavior
Repeated eigenvalues, generalized eigenvectors, and defective cases
Forced systems and variation of constants
Phase portraits and applications
children.description: A phase portrait shows every trajectory at once, making stability and mode interaction visible.

children.title: Nodes, saddles, spirals, centers, and direction of time
Trace-determinant plane for two-dimensional systems
Coupled tanks, circuits, vibrations, kinetics, populations, and physiology
Interpreting dominant modes, time scales, and transient behavior

topics.title: Nonlinear Systems, Linearization, and Stability
topics.description: Nonlinear systems can have multiple equilibria, thresholds, cycles, and behaviors absent from linear models. Local linearization and phase-plane analysis provide a first rigorous toolkit for understanding them without requiring closed-form solutions.

children.title: Phase-plane geometry
children.description: Nullclines partition the plane and help organize the direction field around equilibria and invariant regions.

children.title: Nullclines, equilibria, direction fields, and representative trajectories
Invariant sets, trapping regions, and qualitative sketches
Conservative systems and energy-level curves
Numerical phase portraits checked against analytical structure
Linearization and local classification
children.description: The Jacobian matrix gives the best local linear approximation near an equilibrium and often predicts local behavior.

children.title: Jacobian evaluation at an equilibrium
Hyperbolic equilibria and eigenvalue-based classification
Limits of linearization at centers or zero-real-part eigenvalues
Local versus global stability claims
Nonlinear dynamics and bifurcation awareness
children.description: A small parameter change can reorganize equilibria or generate sustained oscillations, so qualitative transitions matter in applications.

children.title: Predator-prey, competition, epidemic, and autocatalytic examples
Limit cycles and self-sustained oscillation concepts
Saddle-node, transcritical, and pitchfork bifurcation examples
Chaos as enrichment: sensitivity without overclaiming unpredictability

topics.title: Power-Series Solutions and Special-Function Connections
topics.description: Series methods construct local solutions near ordinary and singular points when elementary formulas fail. They also reveal why special functions appear throughout wave, diffusion, quantum, orbital, and cylindrical models.

children.title: Power-series method at ordinary points
children.description: Assuming an analytic series converts a differential equation into recurrence relations for its coefficients.

children.title: Power series, radius of convergence, and termwise differentiation
Index shifting and coefficient matching
Recurrence relations and independent series solutions
Applying initial conditions and estimating truncation error
Regular singular points and Frobenius method
children.description: Frobenius extends power series by allowing a leading fractional or nonzero exponent near certain singular points.

children.title: Ordinary, regular singular, and irregular singular points
Indicial equation and characteristic exponents
Root-difference cases and the possibility of logarithmic terms
Local validity and comparison with numerical solutions
Special functions in applications
children.description: Recurring boundary geometries and coefficient patterns produce named functions that serve as reusable solution bases.

children.title: Bessel functions in cylindrical geometry
Legendre polynomials in spherical and potential problems
Airy, Hermite, or Laguerre functions as enrichment examples
Orthogonality, normalization, and computational evaluation awareness

topics.title: Boundary-Value Problems, Eigenvalues, and Fourier Series
topics.description: Boundary conditions constrain a solution at more than one location and often permit solutions only for special parameter values. This leads naturally to eigenvalue problems, orthogonal expansions, and Fourier representations.

children.title: Linear boundary-value problems
children.description: Unlike an initial-value problem, a boundary-value problem may have no solution, one solution, or many solutions depending on the operator and data.

children.title: Dirichlet, Neumann, Robin, and mixed boundary conditions
Shooting-method intuition and numerical boundary-value solvers
Homogeneous versus nonhomogeneous boundary data
Solvability, uniqueness, and physical interpretation
Sturm-Liouville eigenvalue problems
children.description: Self-adjoint boundary-value problems produce real eigenvalues and orthogonal eigenfunctions that organize solution spaces.

children.title: Operator form, weight functions, and admissible boundary conditions
Eigenvalues, eigenfunctions, orthogonality, and normalization
Expansion coefficients through weighted inner products
Connections to vibration modes, quantum states, and diffusion modes
Fourier series and periodic response
children.description: Fourier series decompose periodic data into sinusoidal modes that linear systems process independently.

children.title: Sine-cosine and complex-exponential forms
Even, odd, half-range, and piecewise expansions
Convergence, endpoint values, and Gibbs phenomenon awareness
Periodic forcing and modal response of linear equations

topics.title: Introduction to Partial Differential Equations and Separation of Variables
topics.description: Partial differential equations describe fields that vary across both space and time. This final unit is a disciplined bridge: students classify foundational PDEs, interpret boundary and initial data, and use separation of variables without pretending to complete a full PDE course.

children.title: PDE models and classification
children.description: The heat, wave, and Laplace equations encode diffusion, propagation, and equilibrium and illustrate distinct mathematical behaviors.

children.title: Deriving conservation-based heat, diffusion, and wave models
Elliptic, parabolic, and hyperbolic classification at an introductory level
Initial conditions and spatial boundary conditions
Well-posedness, units, and physical meaning of coefficients
Separation of variables
children.description: A product assumption turns a linear PDE into linked ODE eigenvalue problems whose modes can be superposed.

children.title: Product solutions and the separation constant
Boundary conditions selecting eigenvalues and eigenfunctions
Fourier coefficients from initial data
Heat and wave equations on a finite interval
Modal interpretation and computational verification
children.description: Modal solutions explain how spatial patterns decay, oscillate, or persist and provide benchmarks for numerical simulations.

children.title: Transient versus steady-state components
Mode shapes, decay rates, frequencies, and energy interpretation
Laplace equation and steady potential as an enrichment example
Comparing truncated series with finite-difference or solver visualizations
